clue.text: Soak fruit one sister's put on

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece put on another sits above it, so these pieces come first

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sister in a religious order is a nun
a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: A recipe step: soak the fruit, then a nun adds her contribution on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places I and NUN above DATE in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to inundate is to flood or drench, as a heavy soak does.

clue.text: Film Etna erupting — fibre's needed

indicators.note: a volcano erupting throws its contents about, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A documentary crew filming Mount Etna in eruption needs some kind of fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges FILM ETNA; Etna is the volcano in Sicily, which suits the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a filament is a fine thread or strand, such as a single fibre.

clue.text: Disturb a person working in US military gallery

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A US soldier based in an art gallery causes a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the soldier's description; the gallery is the London one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to agitate is to stir up or upset, as one may disturb someone.

clue.text: Injury riddle

definitions.meaning: a pulled muscle or sprain, a kind of injury
a riddle is a coarse sieve, and to riddle soil is to sieve or filter it

explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle; here it is the gardener's sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pulled muscle is a wrench-type injury, and sieving liquid or soil is filtering it.

clue.text: Where people go round night and day getting to the heart of problem answers

definitions.text: Where people go round night and day

indicators.note: the inner part of the words problem answers is taken, ignoring their outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone working round the clock to get to the core of a tricky set of answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The French town hosts the 24-hour motor race, in which cars lap the circuit through the night and day.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French town hosts a famous 24-hour endurance motor race, run continuously around a circuit.

clue.text: Fruitful series triumph of one barely running

parts.note: triumph as an adjective, victorious, means winning
to streak is to run naked, and the clue plays on someone doing so

explanation.surface: A naked runner's triumph, with a pun on 'barely'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means scarcely in the surface but is literal here: wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a run of consecutive victories is a productive, rewarding series of results.

clue.text: Oasis panic, greet law roughly

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Panic in the desert as travellers greet a rough frontier law at an oasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oasis' could suggest the band, but it is the desert spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an oasis is a spot in a desert where travellers and animals can drink.

clue.text: Hoaxer going to church in Worcs town

indicators.note: one piece going to another joins it, so they sit side by side

parts.note: a kidder is one who kids, or hoaxes, people
a minster is a large church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: A practical joker sets off for church in a Worcestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcs is short for Worcestershire, an English county in the West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the carpet-making town stands in Worcestershire, on the River Stour.

clue.text: Lines one very good soldier from Down Under cut

parts.note: a saint is a very good person, abbreviated St

indicators.note: the soldier's word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: A poem's lines about a heroic Australian soldier being cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of ANZAC to leave ANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stanza is a group of lines forming a verse of a poem.

clue.text: Item for storing leaves two things on course, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the words are said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: on a golf course, a tee holds the ball and a caddy carries the clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer's kit: two things found on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage, or departs; it is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: a small tin or box in which loose tea is kept is this item.

clue.text: Old bird making endless lament

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to moan is to lament or complain

explanation.surface: An elderly bird making a ceaseless lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like it describes a long lament; it drops the final N of MOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an extinct flightless New Zealand bird, so old in the sense of long gone.

clue.text: Box holding English produce

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it within, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

explanation.surface: A box containing English produce, as at a greengrocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun, fruit and vegetables; it is the verb, to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to create is to make or bring into being.

clue.text: Metal barrel by gents removed

indicators.note: one piece by another sits next to it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

indicators.note: read as re-moved, moved again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Metal barrel taken out of a men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, moved again: an anagram of GENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard grey metallic element, also called wolfram, used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: Animal found in alarming numbers

indicators.note: the letters are found in the run of words alarming numbers, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: An animal appearing in alarming numbers, as in a plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wildebeest, the African antelope, is this animal.

clue.text: Thoroughly fashionable wisdom

parts.note: in means in fashion, trendy
depth of thought or insight is wisdom

explanation.surface: Thoroughly trendy wisdom, as from a guru.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: done comprehensively and in detail, so thoroughly.

clue.text: Woman briefly turning chart over

indicators.note: turning the chart word round, the phrase completed by over, sends it backwards

parts.note: a chart is a map; over rounds off the turning phrase, the chart turned over

explanation.surface: A woman briefly turning a chart upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' belongs to the definition: a short form of a woman's name, Pamela.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form: a pet name for Pamela, a woman's given name.

clue.text: For audience shortly, host gives wave

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: shortly means soon, and a host is an army

explanation.surface: A short welcome: for the audience, the host gives a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like a presenter; it is a great army, as in the heavenly host.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake is this kind of wave.

clue.text: Coach comes up with 'Join together or go under'

indicators.note: in a down light, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a coach is a bus
to merge is to join together

explanation.surface: A team coach's choice: unite the squad, or the club goes under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer; it is the vehicle, a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to submerge is to sink below the surface of water.

clue.text: Quotient resolved, almost

indicators.note: resolved means broken up and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A maths answer: the quotient worked out, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: nearly but falling short, so almost.

clue.text: Live jumps during January Olympic event

indicators.note: one thing during another falls within it, so these letters sit inside
jumping about rearranges the letters of live

explanation.surface: Live jumps on television during a January athletics event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumps' looks like the Olympic jumps but rearranges LIVE into VELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: throwing a light spear for distance is a track and field event at the Games.

clue.text: Fringe breaks record time to show short-lived things

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it so it sits inside

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the edge or fringe of cloth

explanation.surface: A fringe candidate breaks the record time, but it's only short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things lasting only a very short time, such as fads or souvenirs of a moment.

clue.text: Grant immunity to former partner, nearly clear

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to clear a room is to empty it

explanation.surface: A divorce settlement: grant your ex immunity and nearly clear the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exempt is to free someone from a duty or liability.

clue.text: One runs daily or weekly perhaps

definitions.text: One runs daily or weekly perhaps

parts.words: One runs daily or weekly perhaps
parts.note: suggests a jogger's training routine, but the daily or weekly is a newspaper or magazine and the runner its chief

explanation.surface: A keen runner who trains every day or every week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' and 'weekly' are nouns: publications. The person who runs one is in charge of its content.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: the person in charge of a newspaper or magazine runs it.

clue.text: Bottled gas could offer a new energy to get behind yet

indicators.note: these letters get behind the next piece, coming after it

parts.note: yet and but both mean however
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Camping gas could give fresh energy to back a project not yet done.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hydrocarbon fuel sold in pressurised canisters for camping stoves.

clue.text: Vigour this person's displayed after five

indicators.note: one piece displayed after another follows it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
the setter speaking of themself: this person is means I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: Vigour shown after five, as at an evening class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person's' is the setter: I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: energy and enthusiasm are vigour.

clue.text: Entailed adjusting what may be found at top of paper

definitions.text: what may be found at top of paper

indicators.note: adjusting means altering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Adjustments entailed in laying out a newspaper's front page.
explanation.definitionFit: Function: the line giving the date and place of writing heads a newspaper report.

clue.text: Quite a strange one having fled European match

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for one having fled has gone from the words

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A strange one: a European having fled a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having fled' takes I from QUITE A, and 'strange' rearranges what is left into QUATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to equate things is to treat them as equal, to match them up.

clue.text: Going off celeb's heavenly body that's flared up

parts.note: a bomb going off is exploding
a celeb, a celebrity, is a star

explanation.surface: A celebrity going off in a temper, flaring up dramatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nova or supernova, a star that suddenly brightens hugely.
